reasons: Section 2.2 imposes a sole-and-exclusive supplier obligation on Customer for the full term, with no product-category limitation, no 12-month cap and no performance-based exit — this fails the fallback and sits in the stated walk-away zone, so 'deviation' is correctly classified.
The exclusivity runs against Customer (not the acceptable Vendor-side exclusivity), so the detection carve-out does not apply.

The redline reaches the preferred position by converting supply to non-exclusive and confirming Customer's right to source from third parties; the failed minimal-edit heuristic (0.650) is expected here because the rule requires deleting/rewriting the exclusivity commitment, and the edit does not add unrelated terms.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook position and offers the 12-month category-limited fallback with performance exit.

The conflicting Section 12.3 acknowledgement does not cure the problem — the operative covenant in 2.2 remains, and the finding properly flags the inconsistency rather than double-flagging another rule's term.
